newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent gets US boost but wet markets stay blue.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent gets US boost but wet markets stay blue.

text.p: Cash Brent firmed on Wednesday, helped by a smaller than expected rise in U.S. stocks, but North Sea and Mediterranean spot crudes were depressed despite a thinner overhang of March cargoes, traders said.

May Brent gained 10 cents to $20.35 a barrel by 1250 GMT after U.S. crude stocks rose only 76,000 barrels last week against expectations of 2-3 million, and intermonth spreads held onto late U.S. levels, May/June trading twice at +15 cents.
But North Sea wet markets were pinned back on the ropes by ample prompt supply. March 26-28 Brent traded at April Brent less 90 cents, a shade weaker than May-related deals Tuesday.
Brent CFDs also showed little sign of improving, with next week's dates trading at May Brent -39 cents. One April 3-5 Brent cargo was due to turn wet on Wednesday.
Weak differentials for other grades trading late Tuesday confirmed the poor fundamental outlook, traders said.
Ekofisk and Oseberg loading in late March went for Dated Brent less five and 10 cents respectively. But signs that early April differentials were also slipping was more telling, they said.
Early April Oseberg traded at Dated Brent less two cents, down from a two-cent premium last Friday.
In the Mediterranean, refiners shunned offers of Latin American crudes with their normal diet still in ample supply.
Two late March Urals cargoes were on offer. One seller looked for Dated Brent -$1.15 but bids were seen below -$1.30.

Two April-loading Iraqi Kirkuk cargoes, one of over two million barrels, were also on the market, but even after the recent OSP price cut, demand was muted with several local refiners planning maintenance next month.
The U.N. on Tuesday approved two more contracts under the oil-for-food deal, putting the total at 39 since the accord was implemented on December 10.
